resolution.summary: A daylight swatch test on 2026-08-30 tested a warm swatch (tan leather) and a cool swatch (purple/periwinkle tee) side by side against skin. Both read as genuinely flattering — the test didn't resolve warm vs. cool, it resolved that depth/saturation is the governing variable, not hue temperature. Muted or pale colours (a slate-green tee, a pastel sea foam chino) underperformed regardless of temperature. Practical rule: prioritize rich, saturated colour near the face; treat warm-vs-cool as a secondary, low-stakes choice.

swatchTest.method: Six garments/accessories held near the jaw under indirect daylight, same room and window. Pixel brightness was sampled but discarded — smartphone auto white-balance compensated for each swatch's dominant colour, inverting the real signal. Verdict below is a visual read across matched face crops.
swatchTest.verdict: Depth and saturation predict flattery, not warm-vs-cool temperature — a warm swatch and a cool swatch tied for best.

rules.faceRule: Near the face (tops, shirts, knitwear): core neutrals + any colour above at full saturation — warm or cool both work. Avoid muted/dusty or pastel versions near the face regardless of temperature (confirmed by swatch test). Below the waist (trousers, shoes): far more forgiving — existing olive/khaki/camel and pastel pieces (sea foam) all work here.

avoid: triadic and split-complementary as literal 3-hue combos — collapse to two colours plus a neutral instead
